notes:
The Spanish style checks work as they should. Words at the start of a sentence were read as nouns, so the check for three sentences in a row starting with «ella» and the adjective-position check never marked anything, and adverbs were counted as zero in the statistics.

The spellchecker no longer underlines the names of your characters and places: any word in a Story Bible entry's title counts as spelled right, in English and Spanish.

A relationship drawn on the map shows straight away on an entry you had already open, and adding one no longer copies the other entry's links into this one's file.

Clicking a comment's quote takes you to the words it is about and selects them.

More of the Spanish interface is in Spanish: snapshot dates, the built-in compile formats, the Story Bible folder, and headings now in sentence case.

Also: the editor follows each document's language when you switch tabs, the thesaurus no longer mixes a word with a name spelled the same, and new Story Bible files get plain lowercase names.

macOS: Corylus is not notarized yet, so Gatekeeper may say the app cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified. Right-click (or Control-click) Corylus.app, choose Open, then Open again. Only needed once per downloaded copy.
